name: combustion
pattern: A fuel (typically hydrocarbon) reacts with O2 to produce CO2 and H2O. Complete combustion occurs in excess O2; incomplete combustion produces CO and/or C.
conditions: Heat or spark to ignite; excess O2.

name: synthesis
pattern: Two or more reactants combine to form a single product: A + B -> AB
conditions: Often high temperature or pressure; sometimes a catalyst.

name: decomposition
pattern: A single reactant breaks down into two or more products: AB -> A + B
conditions: Heat (thermal decomposition), electrolysis, or photolysis.

name: single replacement
pattern: A free element replaces another in a compound: A + BC -> AC + B (if A is more reactive than B)
conditions: Driven by the activity series of metals; aqueous solution often.

name: double replacement
pattern: Two compounds exchange ions: AB + CD -> AD + CB
conditions: Often in aqueous solution; driven by formation of a precipitate, gas, or water.

name: neutralization
pattern: Acid + Base -> Salt + Water: HA + BOH -> BA + H2O
conditions: Aqueous solution; exothermic.

name: oxidation-reduction
pattern: Electron transfer between species. Oxidation is loss of electrons; reduction is gain. One species is oxidised while another is reduced.
conditions: Varies; driven by electrode potential differences.

name: esterification
pattern: Carboxylic acid + alcohol -> ester + water (Fischer esterification)
conditions: Acid catalyst (H2SO4); heat; often refluxed; equilibrium limited.

name: saponification
pattern: Ester + strong base -> carboxylate salt + alcohol: RCOOR' + NaOH -> RCOO-Na+ + R'OH (soap formation)
conditions: Aqueous NaOH or KOH, heat.

name: hydrogenation
pattern: Alkene/alkyne + H2 -> alkane (or partially to alkene). Adds across C=C or C≡C.
conditions: Metal catalyst (Pt, Pd, Ni); heat; pressure.

name: halogenation
pattern: Alkane + halogen -> alkyl halide + HX. UV light or heat initiates.
conditions: UV light, heat, or radical initiator.

name: hydration
pattern: Alkene + H2O -> alcohol. Markovnikov addition.
conditions: Acid catalyst (H3PO4 or H2SO4); steam; high temperature.

name: dehydration
pattern: Alcohol -> alkene + H2O. Loss of -H and -OH from adjacent carbons.
conditions: Concentrated H2SO4 or H3PO4; high temperature.

name: polymerization
pattern: Monomers join to form a polymer. Addition polymerisation: many alkenes combine without loss. Condensation polymerisation releases a small molecule (often water).
conditions: Initiator, heat, pressure, or catalyst.

name: fermentation
pattern: Sugar -> ethanol + CO2 (alcoholic fermentation) by yeast enzymes.
conditions: Yeast (zymase enzymes); anaerobic; warm temperature; aqueous.

name: Haber process
pattern: Industrial synthesis of ammonia: N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3
conditions: High pressure (150-300 atm), high temperature (400-500°C), iron catalyst.

name: Contact process
pattern: Industrial production of sulfuric acid: 2SO2 + O2 -> 2SO3, then SO3 + H2O -> H2SO4
conditions: V2O5 catalyst, ~450°C; oleum (H2S2O7) is intermediate for safety.

name: Ostwald process
pattern: Industrial production of nitric acid: 4NH3 + 5O2 -> 4NO + 6H2O, then 2NO + O2 -> 2NO2, then 3NO2 + H2O -> 2HNO3 + NO
conditions: Pt/Rh catalyst (first step), elevated temperature.

name: Solvay process
pattern: Industrial production of sodium carbonate: NaCl + NH3 + CO2 + H2O -> NaHCO3 + NH4Cl, then 2NaHCO3 -> Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2
examples: NaCl + NH3 + CO2 + H2O -> NaHCO3 + NH4Cl
conditions: Brine solution; tower process.

name: Wacker oxidation
pattern: Ethylene to acetaldehyde with Pd/Cu catalyst: 2C2H4 + O2 -> 2CH3CHO
conditions: PdCl2/CuCl2 catalyst, aqueous, 50-130°C.

name: Wittig reaction
pattern: Aldehyde/ketone + phosphorus ylide -> alkene. R2C=O + Ph3P=CHR' -> R2C=CHR' + Ph3PO
conditions: Anhydrous, inert atmosphere; non-protic solvent.

name: Grignard reaction
pattern: Grignard reagent (RMgX) + carbonyl compound -> alcohol. R'MgX + R2C=O -> R'R2C-OMgX (then H3O+ -> R'R2C-OH)
conditions: Anhydrous ethereal solvent (diethyl ether or THF).

name: Diels-Alder
pattern: [4+2] cycloaddition of a conjugated diene and a dienophile to form a six-membered ring.
conditions: Heat often; Lewis acid catalyst accelerates.

name: Aldol
pattern: Two carbonyls (often aldehydes or ketones) form a beta-hydroxy carbonyl (aldol addition) which can dehydrate to an alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl (aldol condensation).
conditions: Dilute base (NaOH) or acid; heat for condensation.

name: Cannizzaro
pattern: Non-enolisable aldehydes disproportionate in concentrated base: 2RCHO + OH- -> RCH2OH + RCOO-
conditions: Concentrated NaOH or KOH; no alpha-hydrogens required.

name: Kolbe electrolysis
pattern: Electrolysis of aqueous carboxylate salt gives alkane at anode: 2RCOO- -> R-R + 2CO2 + 2e-
conditions: Electrolysis; platinum electrodes; aqueous solution.

name: Reimer-Tiemann
pattern: Phenol + CHCl3 + NaOH -> salicylaldehyde (ortho-hydroxybenzaldehyde)
conditions: Aqueous NaOH; CHCl3; 60°C.

name: Hoffmann degradation
pattern: Amide + Br2 + 4NaOH -> primary amine with one fewer carbon: RCONH2 -> RNH2
conditions: Aqueous NaOH, Br2, heat.

name: Finkelstein
pattern: Alkyl halide + halide salt (different halogen) -> new alkyl halide. Driven by precipitation or use of excess reagent.
examples: CH3Cl + NaI -> CH3I + NaCl (in acetone, NaCl precipitates)
conditions: Acetone solvent; NaI or KBr.

name: SN1
pattern: Two-step substitution. Tertiary or benzylic halides form a stable carbocation, which is then attacked by a nucleophile. Rate depends only on the substrate.
conditions: Polar protic solvent; tertiary or resonance-stabilised substrate.

name: SN2
pattern: One-step, concerted backside attack. Methyl or primary substrates; nucleophile attacks from the opposite side, inverting the stereocentre.
conditions: Polar aprotic solvent (DMSO, acetone); strong nucleophile; primary or methyl substrate.

name: E1
pattern: Two-step elimination via carbocation, followed by loss of a proton to form an alkene. Competes with SN1.
conditions: Polar protic solvent; tertiary or benzylic substrates; weak base.

name: E2
pattern: One-step, concerted elimination requiring anti-periplanar geometry. Competes with SN2; favoured by strong bulky bases and high temperature.
conditions: Strong base (e.g., t-BuOK); heat; secondary or primary substrates.
